html:
The Pennacook were an Algonquian people of the Merrimack River valley, in what is now southern New Hampshire, northeastern Massachusetts and southern Maine. They were not one united tribe but a network of allied communities. Penacook was also the name of a village at what is now Concord, New Hampshire.

They farmed maize, beans and squash along the river and fished the spring runs of salmon and shad at the falls. In the early 1600s their leader Passaconaway drew many villages together. An epidemic brought by European traders swept the New England coast from 1616 to 1619 and killed a large part of the population.

Passaconaway urged peace with the English settlers of Massachusetts Bay. The Pennacook tried to stay out of King Philip's War in 1675 and 1676, but the war broke them anyway. Many moved north to Quebec and joined the Abenaki at Odanak. They were related to, but not part of, the Wabanaki Confederacy. Their southern neighbours were the Massachusett.
